question: A 50-year-old man has two separate fasting plasma glucose measurements of 118 mg/dL and 121 mg/dL, with an HbA1c of 5.9%. What is the correct interpretation?

answers.text: Diabetes mellitus — both fasting values are elevated

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Diabetes requires FPG ≥126 mg/dL (not ≥100). Both values are below the diagnostic threshold.
Correct. FPG 100-125 mg/dL = impaired fasting glucose (pre-diabetes). HbA1c 5.7-6.4% also falls in the pre-diabetes range. Neither criterion reaches the diagnostic threshold for diabetes.

answers.text: Normal — the FPG and HbA1c are within acceptable limits

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: FPG 100-125 mg/dL is NOT normal — it is impaired fasting glucose. Normal FPG is <100 mg/dL, and normal HbA1c is <5.7%.

answers.text: Inconclusive — repeat the HbA1c on a different day to confirm

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both results consistently fall in the pre-diabetes range. A repeat HbA1c is not needed to establish this pattern; the findings are concordant.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key thresholds: Normal FPG <100, IFG (pre-diabetes) 100-125, Diabetes ≥126 mg/dL. HbA1c: Normal <5.7%, Pre-diabetes 5.7-6.4%, Diabetes ≥6.5%.
Well done — both values place this patient in the pre-diabetes (IFG) category. Lifestyle intervention is indicated to prevent progression.
